newsitem.title: CANADA: Winnipeg is winning war against Red River siege.
newsitem.headline: Winnipeg is winning war against Red River siege.

text.p: Winnipeg on Friday was winning the war against the surging Red River as a massive ditch and miles of dikes withstood the onslaught of the river's crest, but floodwaters were not seen receding for five days.

"The fact it's going up and down shows how well the Red River can be controlled by the Floodway. That tells us for now that we're winning the war," Winnipeg emergency management spokesman Terry Aseltine said.

Winnipeg's Floodway is a 29-mile (47-km) ditch that splits the Red River flood waters as they enter this city of 650,000. The Floodway was built after a devastating 1950 flood forced 100,000 Winnipeg residents from their homes.
The Red River crested at 24.5 feet (7.5 metres) above winter ice level at downtown Winnipeg at 11 p.m. EDT on Thursday.
"The major concern is will the dikes be strong enough to hold," said Aseltine. "We won't be breathing easier for another five or six days," Aseltine said.
The Red River swelled to 22 times its normal flow last month as record-breaking winter snow melted, flooding an area in southern Manitoba twice the size of Hong Kong.
Sandbag dikes burst at two Winnipeg apartment buildings late on Thursday, forcing 242 people from their homes, and breaks were reported at five homes just south of the city.

"As the volume increased, I added pumps. By the time I left I had six pumps going," evacuee Susan Goyer said. "The water just was relentless, coming higher and higher. You'd solve one crisis, breathe a sigh of relief and then turn around to see where the next crisis was coming from. It was just exhausting."
Three other homes were flooded inside the city's southern boundary.
"I was kind of resigned to the fact the dike might breach," Wendy Bloomfield said of the 60,000 sandbags around her home. "But I was surprised it happened so fast. It was only 12 hours."
About 29,000 Canadians and 50,000 Americans have been displaced and four Canadians have died so far in the most extensive Red River flooding since 1852.
Manitoba flood victims received greetings on Thursday from Britain's Queen Elizabeth, who is also Canada's head of state.

"I have read with dismay of the extensive floods in Manitoba," the Queen wrote to Manitobans. "My thoughts are with everyone who has suffered, who is helping those made homeless, or who is battling to prevent further damage."
Winnipeg is also protected by a 25-mile (40-km) dike southwest of the city that was completed on Wednesday, but engineers worried the hastily built structure may not hold.
If so, Red River headwaters could reach Winnipeg in six hours with most of the water reaching downtown in 40 hours.
"Today there's a huge sigh of relief," Winnipeg Mayor Susan Thompson said. "But, boy, I have to tell you, in the next week we have to make sure the dikes are checked."
"If the weather changes, we're right back into very high anxiety," Thompson added.
An additional inch of rain (2 cm) or strong south winds could raise river levels within the city or bring large waves crashing down on 150 miles (240 km) of temporary sandbag dikes.
